perf.summary: DagKthPath.Run and DagLexicographicKthPath.Run are byte-identical; one is redundant.
perf.currentCost: Two separate static classes with identical bodies (the lexicographic variant only differs by a comment assuming sorted adjacency). Duplicated code doubles maintenance and binary/IL surface with zero behavioral difference.
perf.proposedChange: Collapse to a single implementation: have DagLexicographicKthPath.Run forward to DagKthPath.Run (the algorithm is identical; lexicographic ordering is solely a precondition on adjacency-list order, not on the traversal code). Keep both public entry points for discoverability/API clarity but share the body via [MethodImpl(AggressiveInlining)] delegation.
perf.rationale: Removes duplicated logic so a future correctness/perf fix applies to both. Inlined forwarding compiles away under Burst, so no runtime cost. Purely an ergonomics/maintainability win.
perf.risk: None to runtime semantics: the two bodies are character-for-character identical aside from a comment, so the lexicographic guarantee is entirely a caller-side adjacency-ordering precondition. Keep the distinct class names so the documented precondition stays discoverable.

perf.summary: The k<=pathCount[v] selection loop already saturates well; only minor: hoist nothing, but note 'while(true)' is fine and loop is optimal.
perf.currentCost: Each step walks the adjacency list subtracting pathCount[v] until the target child is found; this is inherent O(pathLen * avgDegree) and already minimal. No redundant recomputation present.
perf.proposedChange: No structural change. Confirm pathCount[v] loads are the only memory traffic; they are. Leave as-is. (Reported only to record that the file is essentially optimal and no further opportunity should be invented.)
perf.rationale: The greedy descent is asymptotically optimal for kth-path extraction and already branch-light. Manufacturing micro-opts here would be cargo-cult.
